title: PPA hints read out of a README, and their reconciliation against authority
description: The document `programs/readme_ppa_extractor.py` emits. Every value in it is a HINT: it was read out of a project's own prose, it carries the source span it was read from, and it NEVER overrides an L-doc or an SDC. The document says so in its own body (`authority: HINT`, `authoritative: false`) so that a consumer which read no docstring still cannot mistake it for a measurement. Derived from the documents the program actually emits -- the success path (verdict OK / CONFLICT) and the unreadable-input path (verdict CANNOT_CHECK). See docs/PPA_INTERFACES.md sections 1, 2, 3 and 5.

authority.description: This document's own authority level, and it is a constant. A consumer that finds anything else here is not reading this program's output.

authoritative.description: Always false, in the body, by construction. The guarantee is structural rather than a rule somebody has to remember.

conflicts.description: A hint contradicts an authoritative value at a MATCHED scope. rc=1 -- a finding about the design's own documents.

undetermined.description: The two values were not shown to be comparable. Per PPA_INTERFACES.md section 2 that is UNDETERMINED and never a winner -- and never a conflict.

allOf.description: CANNOT_CHECK is the load-bearing verdict: 'I could not read it' and 'I read it and it was empty' must never produce the same document. It carries a reason, states that it read nothing, and carries no hints -- an empty hint list under an OK verdict is a different fact and stays a different document.

A document that states a verdict ABOUT a README carries the inputs it was run with, the authority it compared against, and its own identity. Without those three a reader cannot tell a run that compared nothing from a run that compared everything and agreed.
CONFLICT is exactly 'at least one conflict', in both directions. A CONFLICT document with an empty conflicts list, or an OK document carrying one, is a document whose summary and whose body disagree.

source.description: The README this document was built from. `sha256` is of the ARTEFACT BYTES, so an auditor reproduces it with `sha256sum`.

span.description: The characters the parser read, and where. Half-open and 0-indexed, so `line[col_start:col_end] == text` always holds and a reader can open the file and see the same characters. A provenance field that cannot be checked is decoration.

hint.description: One (platform, metric) pair and the span it came from.

value.description: Numeric for a counted metric, a string for an identifier-shaped one (a device code, a `WxH` die size), null for a sub-block entry whose count lives under its own key. Never a sentinel: 0 means zero.

platform_key.description: `platform` folded for comparison -- case, whitespace runs and surrounding punctuation are presentation. It is a comparison key, not a normaliser that gets to decide two platforms are the same.

allOf.description: RECORDED means both the span and its digest are there. A hint that claims a recorded span and carries none is the provenance gap this status exists to make visible.
NO_SPAN_RECORDED never invents one. The hint is still emitted -- dropping it would turn a provenance gap into a silently smaller result set.

comparison.description: One hint measured against one authoritative value. `hint_ignored` is a constant and `resolution` is never a decision this program makes: the authority wins by construction.

pointer.description: Where in that file the value is: a JSON pointer for an L-doc, the matched construct for an SDC.

derived.description: A value this program computed rather than read. It carries its formula -- PPA_INTERFACES.md section 3: hash the value you PARSED, and a number you computed is DERIVED and states how.

authority_record.description: One authoritative value harvested from an L-doc or an SDC. A hint is not in this list and can never be added to it.

inputs.description: What the run was asked to do. `rtl_read` is a constant false: this program reads no RTL and says so in the output rather than implying it looked.
